reasoning: While both plans aim to improve trail running speed, Plan B is better suited for the stated goal. It incorporates a wider variety of workouts – hill repeats and tempo runs – which are crucial for developing the specific strength and speed needed for trail running. Plan A focuses almost exclusively on long, easy runs, which primarily builds aerobic endurance but doesn't address the power and speed components essential for tackling varied terrain. The inclusion of harder days with dedicated hill and tempo work in Plan B provides a more comprehensive approach to improving trail running performance.
